paper_title: Hardness of Computing Nondeterministic Kolmogorov Complexity
classifications: Theory of computation → Computational complexity and cryptography
statement: To sum up, pnKt satisfies nearly all pillars of time-unbounded Kolmogorov complexity (as discussed in [28]), which makes the new measure attractive in applications of meta-complexity in time-bounded settings. The only missing property is worst-case symmetry of information, which we leave as an interesting open problem. It is worth pointing out that there is an oracle world where symmetry of information for nKt does not hold (see [29, Corollary 1] and [28, Corollary 6.5.2]).
context: In contrast, average-case symmetry of information does not hold for pKt under the existence of one-way functions [19]. To sum up, pnKt satisfies nearly all pillars of time-unbounded Kolmogorov complexity (as discussed in [28]), which makes the new measure attractive in applications of meta-complexity in time-bounded settings. The only missing property is worst-case symmetry of information, which we leave as an interesting open problem. It is worth pointing out that there is an oracle world where symmetry of information for nKt does not hold (see [29, Corollary 1] and [28, Corollary 6.5.2]). Using a straightforward adaptation of the proof of Theorem 1, we also establish the hardness of MINpnKT, the problem of computing pnKt complexity (we refer to [21, Appendix C] for the precise definition of this problem and the minor modifications needed in the proof). ▶ Theorem 9 (Characterizing NP ⊈ BPP by the Worst-Case Hardness of pnKt ).
